top_choice_rationale: P003 (Cirac, Zoller, Blatt) rewards one bounded achievement: the 1995 proposal of ion-trap quantum logic gates and their realisation in Innsbruck, now reproduced at the highest two-qubit fidelities of any platform after three decades. The credit is a theory pair plus one experimental leader. It is a close call over P001: the Kane-Mele-Molenkamp prediction-and-measurement pairing is sharper, but the omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang removes the theorists who identified the HgTe system, and a citation cannot name who made that prediction. Blatt versus the 2012 laureates is the soft point of P003, and the citation should be kept narrow (gates and computation with laser-cooled ions). P002 is clean on credit but I weigh it as a refinement of the 2005 and 2012 toolboxes; P004 competes for the same Zoller credit and rests on analogue simulation not yet beyond classical reach; P000 is last because several proposals are mature and defensible.
recusal_note: No recusal needed for the slate. I direct WACQT and have documented Chalmers links to Per Delsing, C. M. Wilson and Anton Frisk Kockum, and I recused from B038 (circuit QED), which is not in this slate. WACQT has a general institutional interest in quantum computing, overlapping P003 only at the level of the field; no tie to Cirac, Zoller or Blatt, or to any other credited name, is documented in my profile.
